subject: physics
question_text: State the conditions under which a force does no work.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 6 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty. The TSBIE Basic Learning Material has no VSAQ section for this unit, so the Fastrack is the only source for it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula
lines: Work done by a force is
so W is zero whenever any one of these
steps.margin_note: Start from the formula. The three conditions are just its three factors.
steps.why: Every "no work" case is one of the three factors going to zero. Reading them off the formula means you can never forget one.
common_mistakes: Listing the cases with no formula, so there is nothing to read them off.

recall.must_convey: That W = F S cos θ, so the work is zero when a factor is zero.
accept: W equals F S cos theta
work is force into displacement into cos theta
formula lo edaina factor zero aithe work zero

steps.label: The three cases
steps.margin_note: Three numbered cases. The perpendicular one is the case examiners look for.
steps.why: A porter carrying a load on level ground does no work on it: the force is vertical, the motion horizontal. Tiring is not the same as doing work.
common_mistakes: Giving only "displacement is zero" and stopping.
Saying a force perpendicular to the motion does work because you feel tired.

recall.must_convey: That work is zero when the displacement is zero, the force is zero, or the two are perpendicular.
